messages.subject: Unexpected behaviour in geom_boxplot.
parts:
Hello all,

I am running into some unexpected behaviour with geom_boxplot and I
can't seem to work on what I am doing wrong. I am expecting a boxplot
like this:

airquality %>%
filter(Day<10) %>%
ggplot(aes(x=Month, y=Wind, group=factor(Day), colour=factor(Day))) +
geom_boxplot()

Where there is a box for each value of the x-axis (airquality$Month)
in this case. However, when using my own dataset which has 4 values
for the x-axis (df$Temp1), essentially the same code produces only two
boxplots with no clear indication why. To properly reproduce this I
need to paste a dput() output. That is below. But I did want to ask
can anyone explain why I am experiencing this behaviour? I've aligned
the column class to see if that was the issue but that didn't seem to
fix the problem.

Any help here would be much appreciated.

messages.subject: Re: Unexpected behaviour in geom_boxplot.
parts:
On Fri, Jan 29, 2016 at 12:20 PM, Sam Albers <tonights...@gmail.com> wrote:
df %>%
  mutate(var1=factor(var1), Temp1=as.numeric(Temp1)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=Temp1, y=value, group=var1, colour=var1)) +
  geom_boxplot()

Sam, 

I'm not entirely sure what's going on other than perhaps your grouping variable needs to be a bit "fancier". 

I just did this:

df %>%
  mutate(var1=factor(var1), Temp1=as.numeric(Temp1)) %>%

ggplot(aes(x=Temp1, y=value, group=interaction(Temp1, var1), colour=var1)) +
  geom_boxplot()

and got:


Is that what you're looking for? 

B
